candidateIdentity.variantName: Moonwatch Professional 42 mm, steel on steel

sourceChecks.note: The exact official U.S. product page was independently retrieved on follow-up. It validates the current reference and steel-on-steel configuration, a $7,800 USD manufacturer offer, and structured InStock status; its detailed dimensions and technical facts agree with the exact downloadable product sheet.

The exact official product sheet was independently retrieved on follow-up. It validates identity, steel case and bracelet, 42 x 13.54 x 47.5 mm geometry, 20 mm between-lugs width, approximately 134 g total weight, manual-winding calibre 3861, 50-hour reserve, 50 m water resistance, Hesalite crystal, comfort-setting clasp, and chronograph function.

Omega's official Master Chronometer certification page states a 0/+5 seconds-per-day permitted daily-average range and explicitly includes Speedmaster Moonwatch Professional reference 31030425001001 among the certified watches. This is exact-reference applicability, not a neighboring-calibre substitution.

The exact-reference five-year owner review independently identifies the 0/+5 seconds-per-day Master Chronometer range and reports +4 and +2 seconds-per-day measurements in two positions, corroborating applicability without replacing the official bound. It supplies no controlled lume charge, elapsed-time series, or performance comparison.

Retrieved 2026-08-30 after a narrow Perplexity source-discovery pass. The exact-reference owner identifies marks caused by spring bars while installing the factory bracelet, which is direct configuration-specific secondary evidence but not manufacturer product or service corroboration.

An Omega-certified watchmaker posting in a third-party forum identifies bracelet-to-case part 068ST2207 as a 1.80 mm spring bar for the 3861 bracelet. The technical statement corroborates the exact-reference owner evidence, but the forum is not public Omega service material and does not satisfy the catalogue's manufacturer-corroboration rule.

The exact-reference article establishes Super-LumiNova hour-marker presence but provides no controlled charge duration, darkness interval, brightness comparison, or repeatable grade. Material presence alone cannot resolve lumeGrade.

This mirrored Russian-language manual is an exact-reference operational document and confirms the steel bracelet, comfort-adjustment clasp, and bracelet-length adjustment instructions, but it gives no case-to-bracelet connector or spring-bar specification and no lume performance observation. The mirror is retained as a negative lead rather than manufacturer service corroboration.

The exact-reference review reports +4 and +2 seconds/day measurements and discusses the Nixon bracelet, but contains no controlled lume charge/decay result and does not identify the case attachment mechanism. It cannot close either remaining M1 gap.

The discussion concerns a 3861 Speedmaster Sapphire sibling rather than exact Hesalite reference 310.30.42.50.01.001, and its owner impressions are not a controlled timed test. It is not directly applicable evidence for this variant's lumeGrade.
The exact-reference specification explicitly reports Date: No. A separate exact-reference pre-owned specification independently reports Date display: No.
The exact-reference specification explicitly reports no date display, independently corroborating Watch-Site's categorical no-date field.

This aggregated seller record marks Date as a function, but the same row also misclassifies the exact manual-winding watch as automatic and describes its removable bracelet as fixed. Its visibly unreliable normalized metadata is rejected in favor of two independent exact-reference no-date specifications and Omega's exact product sheet.

Steel bracelet describes the supplied material, not whether the bracelet-to-case interface is spring-bar, quick-release, proprietary, or integrated. Exact-reference owner evidence and a forum post by an Omega-certified watchmaker indicate a spring bar, but no public Omega product or service source corroborates the factory mechanism as required by the acceptance policy.

note: Keep as research-only. Omega's exact product page and product sheet validate the core exact configuration, current $7,800 U.S. in-stock offer, geometry, approximately 134 g total weight, movement, operation, chronograph, and no-date status; the official 0/+5 seconds-per-day bound is independently corroborated. A 2026-08-30 Perplexity-assisted pass found exact-reference owner and Omega-certified-watchmaker forum evidence for a spring-bar bracelet interface, but no public Omega product or service source corroborates the mechanism as required. The exact-reference mirrored manual and a second exact-reference review likewise omit the connector. Exact-reference lume sources establish material presence without a controlled or convergent performance grade; a sibling 3861 owner thread is not directly applicable. Lume and attachment remain the two M1 gaps.
